nodes.summary: Agreement on `e '' K` corresponds to agreement on `K` after transport by `cfgEquiv e`.
nodes.title: Agreement on a set under configuration relabeling

nodes.summary: `agreeOn` is the pointwise form of `Set.EqOn`.
nodes.title: Agreement on a set as pointwise equality

nodes.summary: Agreement on a set implies agreement on any subset (`Set.EqOn.mono`).
nodes.title: Agreement on a set restricts to subsets

nodes.summary: Every configuration agrees with itself (`Set.eqOn_refl`).
nodes.title: Reflexivity of agreement on a set

nodes.summary: `agreeOn` is symmetric (`Set.EqOn.symm`).
nodes.title: Symmetry of agreement on a set

nodes.summary: `agreeOn` is transitive (`Set.EqOn.trans`).
nodes.title: Transitivity of agreement on a set

nodes.summary: `agreeOn K ω ω'`: the configurations `ω` and `ω'` take the same value at every coordinate of `K`. This is `Set.EqOn ω' ω K` (see `StatMech.agreeOn_iff_eqOn`).
nodes.title: Agreement of configurations on a set

nodes.summary: The two point masses of the Bernoulli(`p`) measure add up to `1`.
nodes.title: Bernoulli point masses sum to one

nodes.summary: The product Bernoulli measure of an event is its `wprob` for the Bernoulli marginals.
nodes.title: Bernoulli product measure as a weighted probability

nodes.summary: The scalar inequality behind the induction step of the BK inequality: with `q = 1 - p`, `p, q ≥ 0`, if `c0 ≤ m ≤ a0 b0`, `c1 ≤ a0 b1 + a1 b0 - m` and `c1 ≤ a1 b1`, then `q c0 + p c1 ≤ (q a0 + p a1) (q b0 + p b1)`.
nodes.title: Scalar inequality behind the BK induction step

nodes.summary: The BK criterion: if `C ⊆ ⋃_i P_i ∘ Q_i ∘ R_i` with increasing events, then `P_p(C) ≤ ∑_i P_p(P_i) P_p(Q_i) P_p(R_i)` for the Bernoulli product measure. Reference: J. van den Berg, H. Kesten, "Inequalities with applications to percolation and reliability", J. Appl. Probab. 22 (1985) 556–569.
nodes.title: BK criterion for Bernoulli product measures

nodes.summary: The van den Berg–Kesten (BK) inequality (van den Berg and Kesten 1985): under the product Bernoulli(`p`) measure on a finite configuration space, for increasing events `A` and `B`, `P_p(A □ B) ≤ P_p(A) * P_p(B)`.
nodes.title: Van den Berg–Kesten inequality

nodes.summary: The BK inequality for a product probability weight on a finite set `E`: if `φ ≥ 0` and `φ x false + φ x true = 1` for all `x`, then `wprob φ (A □ B) ≤ wprob φ A * wprob φ B` for all increasing events `A, B`.
nodes.title: BK inequality for product weights on a finite set

nodes.summary: The BK inequality on `Fin n` for a product probability weight `φ`: `wprob φ (A □ B) ≤ wprob φ A * wprob φ B` for increasing `A, B`.
nodes.title: BK inequality for product weights on $n$ ordered coordinates

nodes.summary: `cfgEquiv e` agrees with Mathlib's `Equiv.arrowCongr`.
nodes.title: Configuration relabeling agrees with the library arrow equivalence

nodes.summary: `cfgEquiv e` is monotone.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of configuration relabeling

nodes.summary: The bijection `ω ↦ ω ∘ e` from configurations on `F` to configurations on `E` induced by `e : E ≃ F`. This is `e.symm.arrowCongr (Equiv.refl Bool)` (`StatMech.cfgEquiv_eq_arrowCongr`).
nodes.title: Relabeling configurations along a bijection

nodes.summary: The event that `u` is connected to `B` by an open path inside `A`.
nodes.title: Connection event inside a set

nodes.summary: `u ∈ A` is joined by an open path in `A` to some vertex of `A ∩ B`.
nodes.title: Open connection inside a set to a target set

nodes.summary: `x` and `y` are joined by an open path staying in `A`.
nodes.title: Open connection between two vertices inside a set

nodes.summary: Disjoint occurrence is symmetric: `A □ B = B □ A`.
nodes.title: Disjoint occurrence is symmetric

nodes.summary: The disjoint occurrence of two increasing events is increasing.
nodes.title: Disjoint occurrence of increasing events is increasing

nodes.summary: Disjoint occurrence is monotone in both events.
nodes.title: Disjoint occurrence is monotone in both events

nodes.summary: The notation `A □ B` unfolds to `disjointOccurrence A B`.
nodes.title: Notation for disjoint occurrence

nodes.summary: Disjoint occurrence implies occurrence of both events: `A □ B ⊆ A ∩ B`.
nodes.title: Disjoint occurrence lies in the intersection

nodes.summary: On a one-point configuration space, `A □ B = A ∩ B`.
nodes.title: Disjoint occurrence on a one-point space is the intersection

nodes.summary: The *disjoint occurrence* `A □ B`: the configurations `ω` for which there are disjoint coordinate sets `K` and `L` such that `A` occurs on `K` at `ω` and `B` occurs on `L` at `ω`.
nodes.title: Disjoint occurrence of events

nodes.summary: The event that the edge `{x, y}` is open.
nodes.title: Event that an edge is open

nodes.summary: Union bound from the three-event BK inequality: if `C ⊆ ⋃ i ∈ s, P i □ (Q i □ R i)` with all events increasing and depending on a common finite window, then `P_p(C) ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, P_p(P i) * P_p(Q i) * P_p(R i)`.
nodes.title: Union bound from the three-event BK inequality

nodes.summary: If `A` and `B` depend only on the coordinates in `F`, so does `A □ B`.
nodes.title: Disjoint occurrence preserves finite dependence

nodes.summary: The BK inequality on a countable configuration space: for increasing events `A, B` depending only on the coordinates in a finite set `F`, `P_p(A □ B) ≤ P_p(A) * P_p(B)`.
nodes.title: BK inequality on countable configuration spaces

nodes.summary: Monotonicity in the parameter: for an increasing event `A` depending only on a finite set of coordinates and `p ≤ q`, `P_p(A) ≤ P_q(A)`. The proof uses Russo's formula.
nodes.title: Increasing-event probabilities are monotone in the parameter

nodes.summary: If `A` depends only on `F` and occurs on `K` at `ω`, then it occurs on `K ∩ F` at every configuration agreeing with `ω` on `F`.
nodes.title: Occurrence of a finitely dependent event within its window

nodes.summary: The section on `F` of `A □ B` is contained in the disjoint occurrence of the sections.
nodes.title: Section of a disjoint occurrence

nodes.summary: The BK inequality for three increasing events depending on finitely many coordinates: `P_p(P □ (Q □ R)) ≤ P_p(P) * P_p(Q) * P_p(R)`.
nodes.title: BK inequality for three increasing events

nodes.summary: The indicator of `S` at `Fin.cons x ω'` is the indicator of the slice at `ω'`.
nodes.title: Indicator of an event at a prepended configuration

nodes.summary: For a constant parameter, the inhomogeneous product is `bernoulliProductMeasure`.
nodes.title: Inhomogeneous Bernoulli product with constant parameter

nodes.summary: The product measure on `ConfigSpace E` under which coordinate `e` is open (`true`) with probability `p e`, independently.
nodes.title: Inhomogeneous Bernoulli product measure

nodes.summary: The BK inequality for an inhomogeneous Bernoulli product measure on a finite set.
nodes.title: BK inequality for inhomogeneous Bernoulli measures on a finite set

nodes.summary: The BK inequality for an inhomogeneous Bernoulli product measure on a countable set, for increasing events depending on finitely many coordinates.
nodes.title: BK inequality for inhomogeneous measures on a countable set

nodes.summary: Membership in `A □ B` unfolded.
nodes.title: Membership in a disjoint occurrence

nodes.summary: If `A` occurs on some `K` at `ω`, then `ω ∈ A`.
nodes.title: An event occurring on a set contains the configuration

nodes.summary: If an increasing event `A` occurs on `K` at `ω` and `ω ≤ ω'`, then `A` occurs on `K` at `ω'`.
nodes.title: Occurrence of an increasing event is monotone in the configuration

nodes.summary: Occurrence of `A` on `K` implies occurrence of any larger event `B ⊇ A` on `K`.
nodes.title: Occurrence is monotone in the event

nodes.summary: Occurrence on `K` implies occurrence on any larger coordinate set.
nodes.title: Occurrence is monotone in the coordinate set

nodes.summary: Occurrence is preserved by relabeling the coordinates.
nodes.title: Occurrence is invariant under relabeling coordinates

nodes.summary: If the witness set `K` avoids the first coordinate, occurrence on `K` passes to the `false` slice whatever the value of the first coordinate.
nodes.title: Occurrence avoiding the first coordinate passes to the false slice

nodes.summary: Occurrence on `K` at `Fin.cons false ω'` passes to the `false` slice.
nodes.title: Occurrence with first coordinate false passes to the false slice

nodes.summary: Occurrence on `K` at `Fin.cons true ω'` passes to the `true` slice.
nodes.title: Occurrence with first coordinate true passes to the true slice

nodes.summary: On a one-point configuration space, `OccursOn A K ω` reduces to `ω ∈ A`.
nodes.title: Occurrence on a one-point configuration space

nodes.summary: `OccursOn A K ω`: the event `A` occurs on the coordinate set `K` at `ω`, meaning that every configuration agreeing with `ω` on `K` lies in `A`.
nodes.title: Occurrence of an event on a coordinate set

nodes.summary: The subgraph of `G` of edges open in the configuration `ω`.
nodes.title: Open subgraph of a configuration

nodes.summary: Disjoint occurrence commutes with relabeling the coordinates.
nodes.title: Disjoint occurrence commutes with relabeling coordinates

nodes.summary: The product weight factors over the first coordinate.
nodes.title: Product weight factors over the first coordinate

nodes.summary: A product of nonnegative coordinate weights is nonnegative.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the product weight

nodes.summary: The product weight is invariant under relabeling the coordinates.
nodes.title: Product weight is invariant under relabeling coordinates

nodes.summary: The product weight `∏ x, φ x (ω x)` of a configuration `ω`, where `φ x b` is the weight of value `b` at coordinate `x`.
nodes.title: Product weight of a configuration

nodes.summary: The ordered pairs `(x, y)` with `x ∈ S`, `y ∉ S` adjacent in `G`.
nodes.title: Ordered boundary pairs of a set

nodes.summary: The edge law of inhomogeneous bond percolation: open with probability `1 - exp(-βJ_e)`, closed with probability `exp(-βJ_e)`.
nodes.title: Edge law of inhomogeneous bond percolation

nodes.summary: The edges inside `S`, the boundary edges of `S`, and the edges inside the window `Λ`: the support of the events in the first-exit decomposition.
nodes.title: Support of the first-exit decomposition events

nodes.summary: The `false` slice of `A □ B` is contained in the disjoint occurrence of the `false` slices.
nodes.title: False slice of a disjoint occurrence

nodes.summary: The `true` slice of `A □ B` is contained in `(A₀ □ B₁) ∪ (A₁ □ B₀)`, where `A₀, A₁` are the slices of `A` (similarly for `B`): the first coordinate is used by at most one witness.
nodes.title: True slice of a disjoint occurrence

nodes.summary: For an increasing event, the `false` slice is contained in the `true` slice.
nodes.title: False slice of an increasing event lies in the true slice

nodes.summary: Slices of an increasing event are increasing.
nodes.title: Slices of an increasing event are increasing

nodes.summary: `sliceSet` preserves disjointness.
nodes.title: Removing the first coordinate preserves disjointness

nodes.summary: The coordinate set `{j | j.succ ∈ K}`: `K` with the first coordinate removed, shifted down.
nodes.title: Coordinate set with the first coordinate removed

nodes.summary: The section of an event `C` on `Fin (n + 1)` at first coordinate `x`: the configurations `ω'` on `Fin n` with `Fin.cons x ω' ∈ C`.
nodes.title: Slice of an event at the first coordinate

nodes.summary: A product probability weight has total mass `1`.
nodes.title: Product probability weight has total mass one

nodes.summary: `wprob φ` is monotone for nonnegative weights.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the weighted probability

nodes.summary: Conditioning on the first coordinate: `wprob φ S = φ 0 false * wprob ψ (slice S false) + φ 0 true * wprob ψ (slice S true)`, where `ψ` is `φ` on the remaining coordinates.
nodes.title: Weighted probability by conditioning on the first coordinate

nodes.summary: `wprob` is invariant under relabeling the coordinates.
nodes.title: Weighted probability is invariant under relabeling coordinates

nodes.summary: Inclusion–exclusion for `wprob`.
nodes.title: Inclusion–exclusion for the weighted probability

nodes.summary: The `pweight φ`-mass `∑ ω ∈ S, pweight φ ω` of an event `S`. When `φ ≥ 0` and `φ x false + φ x true = 1` for all `x`, this is the probability of `S` under the product measure whose coordinate `x` has law `φ x`.
nodes.title: Weighted probability of an event

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
